newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela rescuers dig for buried twins.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela rescuers dig for buried twins.

text.p: Omar Barrios believes in his heart that his 5-year-old twins, Gabriela and Beruzca, are still alive under a 6-story office block that collapsed in Wednesday's earthquake.
"I know they're alive, I can feel it," Barrios, 49, told a Reuters correspondent on Friday as he camped out in a plastic tent next to the wrecked Seguros la Seguridad building.
"I'm just waiting for them to be rescued," he added, 43 hours after they were buried by the country's worst earthquake for 30 years.

The Barrios family lived in a first-floor apartment in the office block in Cumana, the historic state capital of Sucre, and the twins were being looked after by 16-year-old babysitter Ismar Maestre, who is also missing.
Firemen have been pumping oxygen down through four stories of broken concrete and wrenched steel in the hope of keeping any trapped survivors alive.

They stopped briefly on Thursday night to listen for telltale signs of life, but after straining for 10 minutes in the enforced silence, geologist Feliciano De Santis told Reuters: "Nothing, there was too much ambient noise."
Twenty-two bodies have been pulled from rubble, and many more are feared buried in the quake that killed at least 68 people in eastern Venezuela, many of them children.
Rescuers said they were going in again to look for the twins, but played down hopes of finding them, or anyone else, alive.
However, said De Santis, "there's always the chance of a miracle, especially for small children who can squeeze into small protected air pockets."
